title: Fastlane
objectives: Understand Fastlane via a real-life analogy
Use lanes, actions, plugins for mobile release automation
Ship builds to Play + TestFlight + Firebase App Distribution
Integrate Fastlane with any CI (Actions, Codemagic, Bitrise)

sections.markdown:
**Think of Fastlane as the Swiss Army knife for mobile-release automation.**

Everything you'd do manually to release a mobile app — bump version, build, sign, upload dSYMs, upload IPA to TestFlight, submit for review, notify Slack, tag git, generate changelog — Fastlane wraps into **actions**. You compose actions into **lanes** (recipes) and invoke them from CI or your terminal.

- **Ruby-based** — Fastfile is a Ruby file; actions are Ruby modules.
- **> 400 built-in actions + community plugins** — Play Store, App Store, Firebase, Slack, changelog, screenshots.
- **`match`** — the crown jewel: syncs iOS certificates + provisioning profiles via an encrypted git repo. No more 'certificate expired' emergencies.
- **`deliver` + `pilot`** — App Store metadata + TestFlight upload.
- **`supply`** — Google Play Console metadata + upload.
- **Cross-CI** — runs on GitHub Actions, Codemagic, Bitrise, Jenkins, local machines.

**Why every serious mobile team uses Fastlane:** iOS signing is a nightmare without it (7 different files that expire, revoke, cross-team-share). Fastlane's `match` alone justifies adoption. Add automated store uploads + Slack notifications + git tagging and the release checklist collapses from 40 manual steps to 1 command.

**Fastlane** is an open-source mobile-release automation toolkit written in Ruby. **Fastfile** declares **lanes** (recipes) composed of **actions** (units of work). Ships 400+ built-in actions covering signing (`match`), building (`gym`, `build_android_app`), uploading (`pilot`, `supply`, `firebase_app_distribution`), notifying (`slack`), and versioning. Cross-platform (macOS + Linux + Windows). Runs anywhere Ruby is available.
## Common actions cheat sheet

sections.markdown: ## A Fastfile for a Flutter iOS release

sections.code:
# ios/fastlane/Fastfile
default_platform(:ios)

platform :ios do
  desc "Sync signing with match (read-only)"
  lane :sync_signing do
    match(type: 'appstore', readonly: true)
  end

  desc "Bump build + tag + push"
  lane :bump do
    increment_build_number(xcodeproj: 'Runner.xcodeproj')
    build_number = get_build_number(xcodeproj: 'Runner.xcodeproj')
    sh("cd .. && cd .. && git add ios/Runner.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj")
    sh("cd .. && cd .. && git commit -m 'chore: bump ios build to #{build_number}'")
    sh("cd .. && cd .. && git push")
  end

  desc "Ship to TestFlight"
  lane :beta do
    sync_signing
    Dir.chdir("../..") do
      sh("flutter build ipa --release --obfuscate --split-debug-info=./symbols --export-options-plist=/tmp/export.plist")
    end
    pilot(
      ipa: '../build/ios/ipa/Runner.ipa',
      skip_waiting_for_build_processing: true,
      changelog: changelog_from_git_commits(pretty: '- %s', number_of_commits: 20),
    )
    upload_symbols_to_crashlytics(dsym_path: '../build/ios/ipa/Runner.app.dSYM.zip')
    slack(message: 'iOS TestFlight build shipped 🚀', channel: '#releases')
  end

  desc "Ship to App Store"
  lane :release do
    sync_signing
    Dir.chdir("../..") do
      sh("flutter build ipa --release --obfuscate --split-debug-info=./symbols")
    end
    deliver(
      ipa: '../build/ios/ipa/Runner.ipa',
      submit_for_review: true,
      automatic_release: true,
      force: true,   # skip HTML preview
      precheck_include_in_app_purchases: false,
    )
  end
end

sections.markdown: ## match — iOS certificate management

sections.code:
# One-time setup:
# 1. Create a private git repo `certificates` (only DevOps + release-eng access)
# 2. Set a strong MATCH_PASSWORD env variable (24+ char); share via password manager.

cd ios
fastlane match init            # asks for URL of certificates repo
fastlane match appstore        # creates + uploads distribution cert + prov profile
fastlane match development     # dev certs

# On CI or new machine:
fastlane match appstore --readonly     # download-only; never generates new

# match stores encrypted cert + profiles in the git repo; MATCH_PASSWORD decrypts on use.
# Rotate MATCH_PASSWORD periodically.

sections.markdown: ## Common mistakes
**Mistake 1: match not `readonly` on CI.** CI creates new certs each run; existing team machines fail. Always `readonly: true` on CI.
**Mistake 2: MATCH_PASSWORD in code.** Set via CI env var; store in password manager.
**Mistake 3: Not encrypting the certificates repo.** MATCH_PASSWORD encrypts; but repo access = compromised anyway. Restrict access.
**Mistake 4: Ignoring 2FA + App-Specific Password for iTunes Connect.** Modern App Store Connect API key eliminates password prompts.
**Mistake 5: Uploading dSYMs manually.** `upload_symbols_to_crashlytics` action + CI.
**Mistake 6: Not versioning lanes.** Fastfile changes untracked → surprises in release. Commit Fastfile changes as PRs.
**Mistake 7: Same lane for internal + external distribution.** Distinct lanes with distinct config.
**Mistake 8: Not running Fastlane locally before CI.** Debugging CI-only failures is painful.
## Best practices
**1. `match` for iOS signing.** No manual certs.
**2. App Store Connect API key** — modern; no password/2FA prompts.
**3. Distinct lanes** — dev / beta / release / hotfix.
**4. Commit Fastfile changes** as PRs.
**5. `readonly: true` for match on CI.**
**6. Automate release notes** from git commits.
**7. Slack notifications** on start + success + failure.
**8. dSYM upload on every iOS build.**
## Practice programs
**Practice 1 (Easy)** — Fastfile with `beta` lane that runs `flutter build ipa`.
**Practice 2 (Medium)** — Set up `match` for App Store cert distribution.
**Practice 3 (Medium)** — TestFlight upload lane with changelog + Slack.
**Practice 4 (Hard)** — Play Store lane via `supply` with staged rollout.
**Practice 5 (Hard)** — App Store Connect API key auth (no password).
**Practice 6 (Expert)** — CI-invoked lane: on tag push → beta → release; with dSYM upload + git tag.
## Interview Q&A

**Q1: Why does every serious iOS release process use Fastlane?**

**A:** **iOS signing is arcane** — 7+ different files (developer certificate, distribution certificate, provisioning profiles, entitlements, App IDs) that expire, revoke, and cross-team-share badly. Manually re-generating them is 30 mins of clicking in Apple's portal, plus updating team members. Fastlane's `match` action **stores all of these in an encrypted git repo**; teammates and CI download via `fastlane match appstore --readonly`. New team member? Run `match` on their laptop; ready in 2 minutes. Cert expired? Everyone auto-updates. Add automated **TestFlight upload** + **changelog from git** + **dSYM upload to Crashlytics** + **Slack notification** and the release checklist collapses from 40 manual steps to `fastlane beta` on your terminal. **Not using Fastlane** = every iOS release involves 30 mins of clicking, 3 emails to teammates about expired certs, and manual copy-paste of release notes. Interviewer signal: appreciating the pain it solves.

**Q2: How does `match` work in detail?**

**A:** **(1) Setup** — create a private git repo `certificates` (only DevOps has access). Set MATCH_PASSWORD env var (24+ char strong). **(2) First run** — `fastlane match appstore` — connects to Apple portal, creates + downloads dist cert + prov profile, encrypts with MATCH_PASSWORD, commits to the certificates repo. **(3) On other machines / CI** — `fastlane match appstore --readonly` — pulls the repo, decrypts with MATCH_PASSWORD, installs into Keychain + Xcode. **Advantages:** (a) one source of truth for signing artifacts; (b) new hires productive in minutes; (c) CI just works; (d) cert rotation is one command. **Trade-offs:** (a) two secrets to manage (repo access + MATCH_PASSWORD); (b) if certificates repo compromised, attacker needs MATCH_PASSWORD too (defense in depth). **Rotation:** `MATCH_PASSWORD` rotated quarterly + certificates rebuilt annually. Interviewer signal: technical depth.

**Q3: When would you use the App Store Connect API key over match?**

**A:** **Apple's App Store Connect API** (v1.0+) supports **key-based authentication** for `pilot`, `deliver`, `supply` — bypasses username/password/2FA prompts. **Use when:** (1) You want CI to run without Apple ID email/password. (2) You need to avoid 2FA interruptions on shared CI accounts. (3) You want fine-grained scope (upload-only vs. metadata-edit). **Setup:** create API key in App Store Connect → download `.p8` file + note key ID + issuer ID → store all three as CI secrets. In Fastlane: `app_store_connect_api_key(key_id:, issuer_id:, key_content:)`. **`match` compatibility:** modern match uses the API key too; no more Apple ID at all. **This is the 2024+ default.** Older Fastlane setups used `FASTLANE_USER` + `FASTLANE_PASSWORD` + `FASTLANE_APPLE_APPLICATION_SPECIFIC_PASSWORD` — hell for 2FA. Migrate. Interviewer signal: knowing the modern path.

**Q4: How would you integrate Fastlane with GitHub Actions?**

**A:** **Fastlane runs on any Ruby-installed machine, including GitHub-hosted macOS runners.** **Workflow:** (1) `actions/setup-ruby@v1` installs Ruby + Bundler. (2) `bundle install --path vendor/bundle` installs Fastlane + plugins. (3) Restore certificates repo via git clone with a deploy key. (4) `bundle exec fastlane ios beta` runs the lane. (5) Secrets injected via `env:` (MATCH_PASSWORD, ASC_API_KEY, FIREBASE_SA_JSON). **Caching:** cache `vendor/bundle` for faster runs. **Trigger:** on push to release/* or on tag. **Alternative:** Codemagic + Bitrise have native Fastlane integration — pass secrets via env-var groups; workflows call `fastlane` command directly. **Cross-CI:** Fastlane is CI-agnostic; same Fastfile runs everywhere. That portability is a huge win. Interviewer bonus signal.

**Q5: What's the difference between `deliver`, `pilot`, `supply`?**

**A:** All three are Fastlane actions for store uploads: **`deliver`** (aliased `upload_to_app_store`) — App Store production. Uploads IPA + metadata (title, keywords, screenshots, review notes) + submits for review. Renamed from `deliver` for clarity. **`pilot`** (aliased `upload_to_testflight`) — TestFlight beta. Uploads IPA + distributes to internal or external testers + optional beta groups. **`supply`** (aliased `upload_to_play_store`) — Google Play Console. Uploads AAB/APK + metadata + staged rollout config (10 % → 100 %). Each uses its store's API + auth. **Combined with `deliver`:** `precheck` action lints metadata BEFORE submission. Interviewer signal: knowing all three by their canonical + aliased names + when to use each.

**Q6: What are common Fastlane mistakes teams make?**

**A:** **(1) `match` not `readonly` on CI** — CI generates new certs, other machines fail. **(2) MATCH_PASSWORD in code** — must be env var + rotated. **(3) Uploading dSYMs manually** — `upload_symbols_to_crashlytics` action solves. **(4) Same lane for internal + external** — different config; separate. **(5) Not committing Fastfile changes as PR** — reviews prevent surprises. **(6) 40-step manual release fallback** when Fastlane fails — invest time in Fastlane instead. **(7) Not running locally before CI** — debug on laptop first. **(8) Ignoring App Store Connect API key** — 2FA/password interruptions plague old setups. **(9) `submit_for_review: true` on every build** — floods Apple review queue; use only on release lane. **(10) No Slack notifications** — silent failures leave the team unaware. Interviewer signal: comprehensive practical experience.

## Real-world usage

- **Every serious iOS team** — Fastlane match is table-stakes.
- **Automated release notes** from git.
- **Cross-CI portability** — same Fastfile in GitHub Actions + Codemagic.
- **Legacy Ruby stack** — Bundler + Gemfile per project.
- **NOT ideal for** — tiny hobby projects (overhead > benefit).

## Advanced notes

- **`Appfile`** — bundle id + Apple ID + team ID; shared config.
- **`Matchfile`** — match config.
- **`Deliverfile` / `Screengrabfile`** — deliver + screengrab config.
- **Plugins** — `fastlane-plugin-firebase_app_distribution`, `fastlane-plugin-git_helper`.
- **`Gemfile` + Bundler** — pin Fastlane version + plugins per project.
- **`sigh`** — provisioning-profile manager (used by match).
- **`cert`** — certificate manager.
- **`scan`** — run Xcode tests.
- **`slather`** — Xcode code coverage.
- **`snapshot`** — automated screenshots.
- **`gym` deprecated** — use `build_app`.
- **`fastlane android` platform** — build_android_app + supply + upload_to_play_store_internal_app_sharing.
- **CI/CD-agnostic** — Codemagic + Bitrise + GitHub Actions + Jenkins.
- **`FASTLANE_HIDE_CHANGELOG` etc.** — CLI flags for CI silence.
- **`before_all` / `after_all`** hooks — Fastfile lifecycle.
- **Multi-platform lanes** — `lane :beta do ... end` inside `platform :ios do ... end`.
